title: Google funds 17 groups to apply AI to scientific research
dek: Google.org is providing $36 million through its Impact Challenge: AI for Science to 17 organizations using artificial intelligence in science.
body:
Google.org announced funding for 17 organizations to use artificial intelligence (AI) , computer systems that perform tasks that normally require human intelligence — to accelerate scientific discovery. The funding comes via the Google.org Impact Challenge: AI for Science and totals $36 million.

## Why it matters

This is one of the larger targeted philanthropic bets linking a major technology company to scientific research via AI. Philanthropic funding can reduce financial barriers for early-stage projects, support development of tools and datasets, and make it easier for researchers and non-profit organizations to pursue high-risk, high-reward work. How the money is allocated and which specific projects receive the grants will shape the near-term research priorities where Google.org is investing.

## The details

- Google.org is awarding $36 million through the Impact Challenge: AI for Science.
- The funding will go to 17 recipient organizations.
- Recipients will use AI as a core part of efforts to accelerate scientific breakthroughs.
- Additional details such as the list of recipient organizations, the specific project descriptions, and the funding breakdown per organization were not provided in the summary available.

## What to watch

Look for the recipient list and project summaries, which will indicate which scientific domains Google.org is prioritizing and whether the grants favor tools, data infrastructure, or direct research programs. Also watch for reporting on measurable outcomes and timelines so funders and the public can assess the impact of the grants.

Source: [Google](https://blog.google/company-news/outreach-and-initiatives/google-org/impact-challenge-ai-science-recipients/)
